RUBY JEAN CHATTO-LUGAGAY Secretary to the Sanggunian Bonifacio, Misamis Occidental Dear Atty. Chatto-Lugagay: This refers to your letter dated December 22, 2023, forwarding the Resolution passed by the Sangguniang Bayan (SB) of Bonifacio, Misamis Occidental - Resolution No. 305-S-2023, entitled: A RESOLUTION RESPECTFULLY SEEKING LEGAL OPINION FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT THRU THE DILG SECRETARY BENJAMIN C. ABALOS, JR. WITH THE INTERCESSION AND ATTENTION OF ATTY. JUAN VICTOR LLAMAS, DILG - LEGAL NATIONAL RELATIVE TO THE NON ISSUANCE OR LACK OF SILG DESIGNATION OF SANGGUNIANG BAYAN MEMBER ALBERTO A. CUIZON DURING HIS TENURE AS ACTING VICE MAYOR OF THE MUNICIPALITY OF BONIFACIO, PROVINCE OF MISAMIS OCCIDENTAL FROM OCTOBER 5, 2022 TO MAY 2023 AND FURTHER INQUIRING ABOUT THE LEGALITY OF THE TRANSACTIONS THAT HAVE TRANSPIRED DURING THE SAID PERIOD. Per the Resolution, on October 5, 2022, Vice Mayor Evelyn C. Dumanjug was preventively suspended for sixty (60) days by the Provincial Governor thru the recommendation of the Sangguniang Panlalawigan (SP) relative to S.P Administrative Case No. 02-22 and eventually a penalty of suspension was also meted for a period of six (6) months. Hon. Alberto A. Cuizon, the ISt ranking SB Member had assumed the Office Of the Vice Mayor during the period of suspension of Vice Mayor Dumanjug from October 5, 2022 to May 30, 2023 based on the Notice to Assume as Acting Vice Mayor issued by the Office of the Govemor, however, there was no authority/designation that was issued from, nor any request forwarded to, the Office of the President thru the Secretary of the Department. Thus, the Resolution submitted to the Department for legal opinion. With such inadvertence, Hon. Cuizon discharged the powers, duties and functions of an Acting Vice Mayor, albeit the lack of a designation from the Department. It is in this regard that we opine that Hon. Cuizon may be appropriately be considered a de facto Acting Vice Mayor. In the case of Arroyo vs. the Court of Appeals and Britoi, the Supreme Court has ratiocinated that: 1 G.R. A judge de facto is one whose acts, though not those of a lawful officer, the law, upon principles of policy and justice will hold valid so far as they involve the interest of the public and third persons, where the duties of the office were exercised: (a) Without a known appointment or election, but under such circumstances of reputation or acquiescence as were calculated to induce people, without inquiry, to submit to or invoke his action, supposing him to be the officer he assumes to be; (b) under color of a known or valid appointment or election, where the officer has failed to conform to some precedent requirement or condition, for example, a failure to take the oath or give a bond, or similar defect; (c) under color of a known election or appointment, void because the officer was not eligible, or because there was a want of power in the electing or appointing body, or by reason of some defect or irregularity in its exercise, such ineligibility, want of power or defect being unknown to the public; and (d) under color of an election, or appointment, by or pursuant to a public unconstitutional law, before the same is adjudged to be such. Xxx Xxx The Court resorts to the de facto officer doctrine to accord validity to the actions of a de facto officer during the period of such officer's wrongful tenure, insofar as the public or third persons are concerned. This principle was born of necessity, as the public cannot be expected to investigate the right of a public official to an office before transacting with them. Thus, on the basis of public policy and convenience, the public may assume that officials are legally qualified and in office. On this basis, it is apparent that the de facto officer doctrine is primarily for protecting those who rely on the official acts of persons discharging the duties of a public office, without being lawful officers. (Emphasis ours) Accordingly, the transactions undertaken during the period when designation order was not issued, we believe, are valid. Nevertheless, for failure to request the designation order, DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2019-212, imposes accountabilities and sanctions thereon. Item Xl states: Non-compliance to the provisions of this Memorandum Circular shall be dealt with in accordance with pertinent laws, rules and regulations. 2 Entitled: OPERATIONAL GUIDELINES AND RULES IN IMPLEMENTING ADMINISTRATIVE ORDER NO. 15, SERIES OF 2018

This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have addressed your concem accordingly. Thank you.
